Subject: Security exhibit: pen-test window and evidence cadence questions

Hi Camila —

Thanks for sending the draft order form. A couple of quick asks from our side as we loop legal:

1) Pen-test window: can Redwood commit to a maximum notice period of 14 days for scheduled pen tests and a rolling 30-day calendar for any emergent testing? Our security team needs clarity so we can align internal change freezes.

2) Evidence cadence: we saw the weekly evidence dump in Appendix A — would Redwood consider a staggered weekly scrub (2–3 artifacts/week) rather than a single weekly package? That reduces our intake burden.

3) SOC 2: can you attach the most recent SOC 2 report and indicate whether Redwood is comfortable sharing SIG or supporting artifacts on request?

We can sign the current order form once we have confirmatory language on the above or reasonable alternative language.

Appreciate it — happy to jump on a short call if helpful.

Best,
Amelia Johnson
Senior Procurement Manager
Novus Health

Hi Amelia —

Thanks, very reasonable asks. Looping in Laura and Karthik from legal/assurance to propose specific, contract-ready language. Quick answers up front:

- Pen-test notice: Redwood can accept a 14-day notice for scheduled pen tests. For emergent tests tied to an active incident we typically reserve the right to coordinate with our customers; we can offer a 30-day rolling window for planned emergent activities (will confirm precise wording).
- Evidence cadence: happy to move to a staggered weekly scrub (we find this workable).
- SOC 2: attaching our latest SOC 2 report now; we can provide SIG-lite on request and discuss narrow artifact sharing under an NDA for sensitive logs.

Proposed next step: Karthik/laura — can you suggest redline language for the MSA Exhibit and Order Form (pen-test notice, evidence cadence, and a short paragraph re: SOC2/SIG access)? If we can get that in the next 24 hours, Amelia, we can route to your procurement/legal and aim to finalize next week.

If you prefer a call instead of back-and-forth redlines, I'm free at 11:30–12:30 PDT.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes

camila_reyes@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Security exhibit: pen-test window and evidence cadence questions

Camila / Laura —

Thanks, Camila. Draft language below (high level; I'll produce tracked changes on the PDF after this thread):

1) Penetration testing / inspection notice
"Vendor shall provide Customer with no less than fourteen (14) calendar days' written notice for any scheduled penetration test affecting Customer's dedicated environment. For emergent testing prompted by an active security incident, Vendor will notify Customer as soon as practicable and will coordinate timing; except where immediate action is required to remediate a critical vulnerability, emergent testing will be scheduled within thirty (30) calendar days of Customer notification. Vendor will use reasonable efforts to minimize disruption and will provide rollback/mitigation plans upon request."

2) Evidence cadence (staggered scrub)
"Vendor will provide security evidence to Customer on a staggered weekly cadence: artifacts will be batched into no fewer than two (2) and no more than three (3) discrete submissions per week, with each submission containing a defined scope (logs, configuration snapshots, or attestations). Parties will agree to a 6-week initial rotation period to confirm scope and adjust cadence as needed."

3) SOC 2 / supporting artifacts
"Vendor will provide Customer with the most recent SOC 2 Type II report. Upon Customer request and subject to a mutually agreeable data sharing agreement (DPA/NDA), Vendor will provide SIG-lite and designated supporting artifacts for specific controls. Vendor is not required to disclose raw production logs unless separately agreed in writing and limited in scope and retention."

Priyom — any operational constraints from evidence delivery or maintenance windows we should flag?

I'll convert to tracked PDF and upload.

-Karthik

Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Camila / Karthik —

Thanks — language looks good overall. A couple of small asks from our security team:

- Can we flip the emergent testing sentence to say "where immediate action is required, Vendor will provide notification as soon as possible and may perform immediate testing with post-facto coordination" — that gives us assurance we'll be informed even if testing is quick.
- For evidence submissions, can we request a single index file per week (CSV or spreadsheet) summarizing the artifacts delivered (type/date/owner) to speed intake?

We reviewed the SOC2 attachment and confirm we'd like SIG-lite and the ability to request a specific artifact set (e.g., control CC5). We'll sign a narrow NDA for artifact transfer.

If you can incorporate the two bullets above into the redline PDF, we should be able to get internal approval and return an executed order form by next Friday.

Best,
Amelia

Quick operational notes to incorporate into the redline (I will produce a combined PDF by EOD):

- Emergent testing: accept Amelia's suggested flip — allow immediate testing where necessary but require post-test report and corrective action plan within five (5) business days.
- Index file: fine — we'll provide a single CSV index for each week's deliveries and include a short description and retention window for each artifact.
- Evidence delivery mechanics: recommend we specify S3-signed-URL delivery or secure share link with 30-day access by default; any long-term retention requests will require a separate agreement.

Action items: Karthik to author the tracked PDF with the adjusted emergent-testing sentence and the staggered-submission wording; Priyom will append the operational appendix (index template + delivery mechanics); Camila to run with Novus for signoff and confirm NDA step for SIG-lite.
